reason: Durable branch handles must carry the allocation identity so reopen, destroy, and plan application can reject a locator swapped between allocations that share a branch name. This intentionally breaks callers constructing durable handles directly; they should use branchDurable or reopenDurableBranch.
A persisted descriptor must identify its physical allocation independently of the reusable branch name. Existing descriptors must be recreated so reopen and destroy can reject locator substitution.
The host attestation must include allocation identity so descriptor comparison rejects a different working copy with the same branch name. Hosts must persist this field for new allocations.

A host-native merge that commits internally can bypass the target Store transaction's revision fence. Durable plans now apply through that transaction; native databases may still provide the working copy.
The native merge result type was retired with the unsafe host-native merge callback. Plan application now returns the portable Store merge result.
